verdicts.title: Sliding-window constraint silently dropped under SDPA when attention_mask is None
verdicts.reasoning: Reproduced end to end. masking.py:76-82 returns None whenever attention_mask is None, _attn_implementation != 'eager' and the cache is empty, with no sliding_window consideration; masking.py:226-227 propagates that None out of vmap_create_sliding_window_causal_mask. Direct call check: with a config carrying _attn_implementation='sdpa', sliding_window=4, inputs_embeds (1,12,8) and attention_mask=None the function returns None, while the same config with 'eager' returns a mask whose last query row allows only keys [8,9,10,11] (a correct 4-wide window). Full-model repro (uv run, transformers 5.16.1): tiny MistralForCausalLM, sliding_window=4, sdpa, input (2,12). Upstream logits are identical with and without an all-ones attention_mask (diff 0.0), i.e. upstream honours the window in both cases -- consistent with masking_utils.py:261-263, which returns False from _can_skip/_ignore when 'local_attention_size is not None and kv_length >= local_attention_size'. After apply_transformers_model_patches(model, eager_attention=True) the patched model matches upstream exactly with a mask (0.0) but deviates by 0.158 max-abs without one (reporter measured 0.39 on a different random config; same defect, magnitude is config-dependent). Reachability: the patched model-level masking rebind (components/masking.py) installs the shim in every registered family module, and DPTrainer keeps SDPA on CUDA/CPU (only _workaround_mps_bf16_sdpa forces eager, and only for bf16 on MPS). The opaque SFT collator always emits attention_mask (sft/collator/_language_modeling.py builds attention_mask_t unconditionally), so opaque-collated training is safe, but DPTrainer passes the batch through as-is and explicitly tolerates batches without attention_mask (_dp_trainer.py:1809, 1827), so pre-packed fixed-length datasets and any plain model(input_ids) eval/prefill call hit the bug. No test covers it: every sliding-window case in tests/transformers/runtime/test_masking.py sets _attn_implementation='eager' (lines 115, 119, 125, 215). Line citations are accurate. Utility/correctness only, no sensitivity or accounting impact, so affects_epsilon=false is right. Not a duplicate: the only related tracker, #330 ('Establish patched-versus-upstream numerical parity'), was closed as completed on 2026-08-27 (after the open-issue snapshot) and this is a live code defect in masking.py, not parity infrastructure.
verdicts.corrected_failure_scenario: A patched sliding-window family (Mistral/Ministral, Gemma2, Gemma3 text, Cohere2, Phi-3) runs with attn_implementation='sdpa' (the transformers default) and no attention_mask, on a prefill/no-cache call with seq_len >= sliding_window: vmap_create_causal_mask returns None, vmap_create_sliding_window_causal_mask forwards the None, SDPA falls back to is_causal=True, and sliding layers attend to the entire context instead of the last `sliding_window` tokens. Verified on tiny Mistral (sliding_window=4, seq=12, sdpa): patched no-mask logits differ from upstream by 0.158 max-abs while the masked path matches upstream bit-for-bit. Reachable both from plain model(input_ids) eval/perplexity/generation-prefill code and from DPTrainer when the batch carries no attention_mask (pre-packed datasets); the opaque SFT collator always emits one, so its own flows are unaffected. Privacy accounting is untouched -- the harm is silently training/evaluating a model whose attention pattern differs from the architecture it claims to implement.

verdicts.title: #495 quietly reverted #493's fail-closed dropout/batchify contract for default (trainer) calls
verdicts.reasoning: Every factual claim checks out, but the framing overstates the harm. Git history: 6e26cc97 ('fix(patches): apply router dropout and batchify consistently (#493)') introduced 'if dropout or batchify: raise ValueError' on the unregistered-family path; 2b309916 ('fix(ci): separate Python and Rust test gates ... (#495)') added dropout_explicit/batchify_explicit and narrowed the raise to '(dropout_explicit and dropout) or (batchify_explicit and batchify)' -- the diff really is inside a CI-titled commit that also touched two TRL compat tests. Current code is _router.py:116-135 as cited. Behaviour reproduced: a tiny FalconForCausalLM (unregistered family) through opaque.patches.apply_model_patches(m) with defaults raises nothing, logs only 'DEBUG opaque.api.patches.transformers._router: no registered apply function for model family falcon', and leaves nn.Dropout p=0.3 untouched. DPTrainer does call apply_model_patches with only compat/performance/kernels (_dp_trainer.py:802-808) so it takes exactly this path, and its docstring still promises an 'info-level message' (:791-793) while the code logs debug. randomness='same' is confirmed at packages/opaque-engine/src/opaque/api/engine/clipping/_clipped_fun.py:310 (the finding cites _clipped_fun.py:310, right line, slightly different path). Downgrade to low because the relaxation was not a stealth regression of a needed guard: #493's version raised for ANY model whose family is unregistered under the default compat=True, which includes the plain nn.Module / custom fixtures DPTrainer explicitly documents as supported (same docstring, 'set use_compat_patches=False to suppress for custom or non-HF nn.Module fixtures'). The residual defect is therefore narrow -- an inconsistent contract for unregistered HF families plus a debug-vs-info log-level and docstring mismatch. No privacy impact: per-example clipping still bounds sensitivity regardless of dropout. Existing tests (tests/transformers/components/test_dropout.py:56-88) pin only the explicit-kwarg raise and a compat=False no-raise; the default-compat unregistered path is untested. No open tracked issue covers it (#400 is closed).
verdicts.corrected_failure_scenario: A user trains an HF model of an unregistered family (e.g. Falcon) through DPTrainer with defaults: apply_model_patches returns silently after a debug-level log, no compat patches are applied, and the model's dropout stays enabled (verified: nn.Dropout p stays 0.3 on a tiny Falcon). Under vmap(grad) with randomness='same' the surviving dropout mask is shared across every example in the batch, so gradients differ from both standard training and the dropout-free configuration the trainer documents. Privacy is unaffected. The user-visible defects are the missing signal (debug, while DPTrainer's docstring promises info) and the inconsistent contract between the explicit and default kwarg paths -- not a plain revert, since raising on the default path would break the custom/non-HF nn.Module models DPTrainer documents as supported.

verdicts.title: Parity suite's 'upstream' reference is contaminated by unreverted module-global patches after the first test per family
verdicts.reasoning: Reproduced. _test_utils.py:255-272: parity_model_patches snapshots {type(module): type(module).forward} and restores only those class attributes in the finally block. apply_transformers_model_patches -> family apply (_family.py:166-184) additionally rebinds mod.repeat_kv, mod.eager_attention_forward, mod.ALL_ATTENTION_FUNCTIONS['sdpa'] (gemma2 only) and, via apply_module_masking_patch, mod.create_causal_mask / mod.create_sliding_window_causal_mask -- none restored. Direct check on modeling_llama after 'with parity_model_patches(model): pass': eager_attention_forward is vmap_eager_attention_forward (not restored), create_causal_mask is vmap_create_causal_mask (not restored); class forwards and the sdpa registry entry are restored (llama passes sdpa_attention_replacement=None). There is no conftest under tests/transformers/models that resets state -- the only autouse fixture lives in tests/transformers/components/conftest.py. Consequence is real: test_parity parametrizes attn_impl over eager and sdpa, so once any test has touched a family module every later 'unpatched' reference of that family builds masks with opaque's builders and, in the eager lane, runs opaque's eager_attention_forward/repeat_kv -- patched-vs-patched. This weakens the parity guarantee that closed #398/#397/#404 rest on. Medium, not high: it is a test-integrity defect with no runtime effect, and today's assertions still pass because the shims are numerically equivalent on the inputs used. Not a duplicate of an open issue -- #330 (the parity tracker) was closed completed on 2026-08-27, and this names a specific defect in the delivered harness rather than the umbrella goal.
verdicts.corrected_failure_scenario: Within one pytest process, the first parity test to run for a family permanently rebinds that family's module globals (eager_attention_forward, repeat_kv, create_causal_mask, create_sliding_window_causal_mask); parity_model_patches restores only class-level forwards. Every subsequent 'unpatched' reference model of that family therefore runs opaque's attention and mask builders, so the backward-grad, vmap-grad, sliding-window, softcapping and KV-cache comparisons -- and in particular the whole eager attn_impl lane -- largely compare patched against patched. A future regression inside vmap_eager_attention_forward, vmap_repeat_kv or the mask builders that shifts reference and patched numerics identically would pass the suite, leaving only the first forward-logits test per family as genuine upstream comparison. Verified by inspecting modeling_llama's globals after the context manager exits.

verdicts.title: test_sliding_window_parity never exercises a binding window (sliding_window=64 > seq_len=10)
verdicts.reasoning: Code confirmed verbatim: test_parity.py:295-313 sets extra['sliding_window'] = 64 and calls assert_parity_forward, which builds input_ids of shape (2, 10) and attention_mask = torch.ones_like(input_ids) (_test_utils.py:352-355). With absolute query positions 0..9 and a 64-wide window, the look-back bound q_abs - 63 is always <= 0, so window_in_mask (masking.py:271-273) is all-True and the sliding constraint contributes nothing -- the test is numerically identical to test_forward_parity for mistral/ministral (_SLIDING_WINDOW_FAMILIES at test_parity.py:56). The harness always supplies a mask, so it also cannot reach the confirmed no-mask SDPA skip (finding 42). Downgraded to low: this is a pure coverage gap with no live defect behind the specific path it fails to cover -- I verified that with a genuinely binding window (sliding_window=4, seq=12) and an attention_mask present the patched Mistral matches upstream bit-for-bit (diff 0.0), so a binding-window variant of this test would pass today rather than expose a bug. Its value is guarding future boundary regressions. Not tracked by any open issue (#330 closed completed 2026-08-27).
verdicts.corrected_failure_scenario: test_sliding_window_parity configures sliding_window=64 while the shared harness feeds sequences of length 10 with an all-ones attention_mask, so the look-back constraint never excludes a single key and the test degenerates into a duplicate of test_forward_parity for mistral and ministral. A future off-by-one or dropped-constraint regression in vmap_create_sliding_window_causal_mask's window bound would pass unnoticed, and because the harness always passes a mask the confirmed no-mask SDPA window drop is out of reach as well. No current defect is hidden by this specific gap -- with a binding window and a mask the implementation matches upstream exactly (verified at sliding_window=4, seq=12).

verdicts.title: Gemma2 SDPA shim is installed in the process-global attention registry, rerouting every model family
verdicts.reasoning: Reproduced. _family.py:176-180 (finding cites 172-176; off by four lines, same statement) does mod.ALL_ATTENTION_FUNCTIONS['sdpa'] = sdpa_attention_replacement, and only gemma2.py passes one (vmap_sdpa_attention_forward_gemma2). transformers 5.16.1 defines a single AttentionInterface instance (modeling_utils.py:5177) that every modeling module imports; GeneralInterface.__setitem__ (utils/generic.py:1117-1119) writes that instance's _local_mapping, and get_interface (modeling_utils.py:5161-5173) reads through it. Verified at runtime: modeling_llama.ALL_ATTENTION_FUNCTIONS is modeling_gemma2's and modeling_utils' (identity True), and after apply_gemma2_family_patches() llama's 'sdpa' entry is vmap_sdpa_attention_forward_gemma2. The shim delegates verbatim to stock sdpa_attention_forward when softcap is None (components/attention.py:172-196), so most families are unaffected numerically, but t5gemma, vaultgemma and videoprism pass softcap=self.attn_logit_softcapping into the interface in 5.16.1 and upstream sdpa_attention_forward swallows it in **kwargs. Empirically confirmed with two subprocesses using identical weights: an unpatched tiny VaultGemma (attn_logit_softcapping defaults to 50.0) with sdpa produces logits differing by 0.290 max-abs when gemma2 family patches were applied earlier in the process versus a clean process. Low severity is right: it needs a second, unrelated softcapped-Gemma-variant model in the same process, the override is never restored, and the patched model itself is unaffected. Same defect class as the closed #396; nothing open tracks it.
verdicts.corrected_failure_scenario: A process applies opaque's gemma2 family patches (any Gemma2 model through apply_model_patches), which writes vmap_sdpa_attention_forward_gemma2 into the single process-wide AttentionInterface shared by every transformers modeling module. Any unpatched model loaded afterwards with attn_implementation='sdpa' now dispatches through the shim. For softcap=None callers this is a verbatim delegation, but for families that forward softcap into the interface -- vaultgemma (attn_logit_softcapping defaults to 50.0), t5gemma, videoprism -- the shim diverts to opaque's Gemma2 eager attention, applying softcapping that upstream SDPA ignores and materializing attention weights. Verified: an unpatched tiny VaultGemma with identical weights yields logits 0.290 max-abs apart between a clean process and one where apply_gemma2_family_patches() ran. The override is never reverted for the life of the process.

verdicts.title: Fused activation backward still mutates saved gate/up activations in place (residual of #401/#402 pattern)
verdicts.reasoning: Static chain verified; runtime reproduction impossible here (torch.cuda.is_available() is False, so the Triton kernels cannot execute). Opaque_LoRA_MLP.setup_context (lora.py:1121-1133) saves gate and up -- which are also forward outputs -- via ctx.save_for_backward; backward (lora.py:1141-1166) hands them to _LoRAMLPBackward/_LoRAMLPBackwardLite, whose impl reshapes them into gate_flat/up_flat (lora.py:747-748, storage-sharing views) and calls _ACTIVATION_BACKWARD_FUSED (lora.py:757-759). _triton_swiglu_backward_fused (swiglu.py:370-400) documents and performs exactly the aliasing overwrite 'dh -> h, gate -> dgate, up -> dup', passing gate_flat/up_flat as both input and output pointers; _SwiGLUBackward.forward (swiglu.py:145-160) does the same. git show 96cf21d1 (#482) confirms the fix removed only the out=X_flat / dX-into-X storage reuse and left the gate/up overwrite intact by design ('Unsloth pattern'). Because the write happens inside a Triton kernel it bypasses the dispatcher, so no version-counter bump and no autograd error. What remains unverified: that a second traversal actually yields wrong numbers rather than an unrelated failure -- this needs a CUDA+Triton host. Exposure is narrow: the caller discards the returned gate/up (peft/components/mlp.py:70), the DP-SGD vmap(grad) path builds a fresh graph per call, double backward already raises NotImplementedError, and no code in the repository or its tests uses retain_graph with these kernels. Hence low, not medium. Not covered by any open issue (#401/#402 closed).
verdicts.corrected_failure_scenario: On a CUDA+Triton host with fused LoRA MLP kernels installed, the first backward overwrites the autograd-saved gate/up activations with dgate/dup inside a Triton kernel, bypassing the tensor version counter. A caller that re-traverses the same graph -- loss.backward(retain_graph=True) followed by another backward, or two torch.autograd.grad calls with retain_graph=True -- then recomputes the activation backward from gradient values instead of activations, producing silently wrong dX and LoRA weight gradients with no exception. Not reached by opaque's own DP-SGD path (fresh graph per vmap(grad) call, gate/up discarded by the PEFT MLP forward, no retain_graph use anywhere in the tree); the numerical consequence was not executed here because the environment has no CUDA.
